verdict.rationale: three.js is a rendering library — no evidence of any built-in physics engine (rigid bodies, collisions, raycasts as physics) shipped out of the box; evidence only covers rendering (WebGL/WebGPU), loaders, and controls. Raycaster exists in three.js for picking but no physics/collision system is documented, and physics is a well-known gap requiring third-party libraries like Cannon.js or Ammo.js.
